bills.title: To name the Department of Veterans Affairs community-based outpatient clinic in San Jose, California, as the "Corporal Patrick D. Tillman VA Clinic".
bills.status: Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4288 is a VA facility-naming bill that does not touch any Treasury authority, tax provision, or appropriations mechanism. Treasury has no implementation role or financial risk exposure here, and no legislative affairs engagement is warranted.

bills.title: To require the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to review and update Federal Aviation Administration regulations, policies, and guidance related to low-altitude airspace safety, and for other purposes.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9695 does not appear to have a direct nexus to Treasury's statutory authorities, appropriations, or program equities based on the information provided. If a specific Treasury connection exists, such as IRS unmanned aircraft surveillance use, FinCEN-related drone activity, or Secret Service airspace coordination funded through Treasury accounts, that context would be needed to identify the relevant office and implementation risk.

bills.title: Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9289 falls squarely within Treasury's jurisdiction because it would likely modify or restrict the tax treatment of education savings accounts or school-choice related tax provisions administered by IRS under the Internal Revenue Code. Treasury and IRS would bear the implementation burden of any new compliance requirements or reporting rules, and any restriction on existing tax benefits carries revenue-scoring implications that the Office of Tax Policy would need to assess.

bills.title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that President Donald Trump, his Special Envoy Steven Witkoff, and all Federal officials must comply with the Foreign Emoluments Clause of the Constitution by immediately turning over to the Department of the Treasury any payments received from the United Arab Emirates or any other foreign state and divest from all business interests linked to foreign governments.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
bills.nexus: H.Res. 1186 directly names the Department of the Treasury as the designated recipient of any foreign-government payments that covered officials are required to surrender, making Treasury a named operational actor in any compliance mechanism the resolution envisions. Although the measure is a non-binding sense-of-the-House resolution with no immediate legal force, Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control and General Counsel would need to assess whether existing authorities support accepting and accounting for such remittances, and the resolution could foreshadow binding legislation imposing those obligations.

bills.title: Defending the Human Rights of Palestinian Children and Families Living Under Israeli Military Occupation Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because the bill's restrictions on U.S. assistance could implicate OFAC-administered foreign assistance fund flows and any conditions tied to financial transfers involving Israeli government or military entities. The implementation risk lies in potential ambiguity around whether existing sanctions frameworks or export-finance mechanisms administered by Treasury would need to be revised to comply with new congressionally mandated restrictions.

bills.title: Mexican Energy Trade Enforcement Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5926 falls within Treasury's purview because trade enforcement mechanisms, including tariffs and customs revenue collection, are administered through Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and coordinated with U.S. Customs and Border Protection under Treasury's broader revenue authority. The implementation risk centers on potential retaliatory measures from Mexico that could disrupt existing energy trade flows and complicate Treasury's role in managing any related financial sanctions or duty collection frameworks.

bills.title: No Tax on Overtime for All Workers Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5475 would exclude overtime pay from federal taxable income, directly affecting the Internal Revenue Service's administration of individual income tax under Treasury's Tax Policy and IRS oversight authorities. Treasury faces significant revenue-loss risk and substantial implementation burden, as IRS would need to redesign withholding tables, update Form W-2 reporting, and ensure employer compliance across millions of payroll systems.

bills.title: America’s Olympic and Paralympic Games Commemorative Coins Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4382 directly engages the U.S. Mint, a Treasury bureau, which would be authorized and required to design, produce, and issue commemorative coins under the bill. Treasury's implementation risk centers on minting capacity, surcharge distribution logistics, and ensuring the program does not result in a net cost to the government as required by the Commemorative Coin Reform Act of 1996.

bills.title: Generating Retirement Ownership through Long-Term Holding
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2089 falls within Treasury's purview because it would modify retirement savings provisions of the Internal Revenue Code, directly implicating the Office of Tax Policy and IRS rulemaking authority. The implementation risk centers on revenue scoring, plan qualification rules, and potential complexity in administering new long-term holding incentives across defined-contribution plan structures.

bills.title: Expressing the sense of Congress that tax-exempt fraternal benefit societies have historically provided and continue to provide critical benefits to the people and communities of the United States.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.Con.Res. 4 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and IRS Tax Exempt and Government Entities division, which administer the IRC Section 501(c)(8) exemption framework for fraternal benefit societies. Although a sense-of-Congress resolution carries no binding legal effect, it can signal congressional intent to resist future IRS guidance or legislative proposals that would tighten exemption standards or reporting requirements for these entities.
